discovery: Theory and realization of the self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE) X-ray free-electron laser

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

motivation: The X-ray free-electron laser is the most transformative new light source since the synchrotron. Saldin (with Kondratenko) and Pellegrini (with Bonifacio and Narducci) showed that a relativistic electron beam in a long undulator can amplify its own spontaneous emission collectively, exponentially, from noise, making a laser at X-ray wavelengths possible without mirrors. Kim developed the rigorous theory of SASE start-up, transverse coherence and gain, and with Pellegrini championed the design that became LCLS. Since 2009, LCLS, FLASH, SACLA, European XFEL and SwissFEL have delivered femtosecond X-ray pulses a billion times brighter than any earlier source. This has opened ultrafast X-ray spectroscopy and scattering, time-resolved structural biology, warm-dense-matter physics and nonlinear X-ray optics. It is a clear case of basic physics insight turned into an instrument used by thousands of scientists across physics, chemistry and biology.
